problems.title: Actual-menu normalization creates higher-order effects in one layer
problems.source_location: Sections 2.2 and 3.2, current arXiv v1 PDF pp.3 and 5–6, Eqs.(4)–(5)
claim: The feature-based architecture averages over actual menu size and asserts that layer l has interaction effects only through order l under its subset decomposition.
analysis: Use scalar features \(x=(1,2,3,4)\), one layer/head, unit weights, and ReLU encoders/modulators acting identically on these positive features. The specified utility is \(u_j(S)=x_j[1+\sum_{k\in S}x_k/|S|]\). For the always-present pair \(1,2\), log odds on menus \(12,123,124,1234\) are \(-5/2,-3,-10/3,-7/2\). The mixed difference for optional items 3 and 4 equals \(-7/2+3+10/3-5/2=1/3\). First-order relative utilities must have zero such difference. The observable odds eliminate any common utility-shift ambiguity.
result: The one-layer interaction-order upper bound is false over the stated variable-menu domain. Permutation equivariance survives; a fixed-cardinality empirical slice does not establish the required subset identities.
repair: Replace actual-size normalization by a fixed positive constant and mask all invalid contributions. With base-only modulators and linear aggregation/readout, Boolean menu-membership degree increases by at most one per layer, proving the repaired order upper bound.
problems.impact_rationale: The exact observable second-order effect directly contradicts the architecture’s central claim of controlling interaction order by depth.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Padded alternatives enter the context summary
problems.source_location: Appendix B.2, current arXiv v1 PDF p.18; Model/FeatureBased.py, DeepHalo.forward, lines 63–76
claim: The appendix says dummy states are reset to zero after residual layers and do not affect aggregation. The release sums all affine projected states before applying a valid-item mask only to the modulator.
analysis: A zero raw feature need not have zero embedding after biased layers and normalization. Even if its state were zero, an affine aggregate projection contributes its bias. With projection weight zero and bias one, five slots containing two real items produce unmasked summary \(5/2\), versus the correct masked summary \(1\). Item-specific modulators can turn that difference into unequal valid-logit changes; final dummy softmax masking cannot remove prior context contamination.
result: The released class violates the specified dummy noninterference. Actual real-data training paths/checkpoints are not available to quantify the published effect.
repair: Mask embeddings and residual states, and mask after each affine aggregate projection before summing. This gives padding invariance by induction for deterministic evaluation.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a released feature-model masking discrepancy with unmeasured correspondence to the published real-data experiments.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Named baseline descriptions differ from the cited models
problems.source_location: Appendix C.2.2, current arXiv v1 PDF p.20; RUMnet Section 2.3; TasteNet-MNL Section 3.1
claim: The appendix describes RUMnet as an alternative-order GRU and TasteNet as deriving user representations from mean offered-item features, while interpreting the comparison as involving context-independent approaches.
analysis: The cited RUMnet uses shared feed-forward component utilities, per-component softmax and probability averaging, not an item-order GRU. A scalar GRU recurrence \(h_t=h_{t-1}/2+\tanh(x_t)/2\) can change matched item utility differences when order reverses. Original TasteNet maps fixed consumer characteristics to taste coefficients; replacing those with menu mean changes the object. For the described scalar dot product \(u_j=x_j\bar x_S\), log odds of features 1 and 2 change from \(-3/2\) to \(-2\) when feature 3 is added.
result: The published baseline specifications are different from the cited architectures. Missing baseline training implementations leave open whether the code or the descriptions need correction; no table ranking is recalculated.
repair: Identify and release the actual baseline architectures/inputs and distinguish adapted models from the named originals; rerun faithful versions if the intended comparison is to those originals.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a concrete baseline attribution/specification discrepancy, with actual trained model identity and numerical consequences unresolved.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

impact_rationale: Major: the claimed layer-by-layer interaction-order control fails even in observable log odds of an allowed one-layer model.
